title: Port to City
dek: Ten source-linked records trace a working relationship between harbour, street and district. The value is not any one photograph. It is the chain between them.

chapters.title: Harbour and city in one field
chapters.intro: Early aerial records hold water, infrastructure and urban fabric in the same view. They establish the spatial question before interpretation begins.

chapters.title: The working edge at street level
chapters.intro: Rue de la Commune, Bonsecours and Place d'Armes move the evidence from city scale to the places people occupied and crossed.

chapters.title: Port reports, not isolated images
chapters.intro: The mid-century material belongs to dated report sequences. That relationship makes the quays, warehouses and circulation legible as a system.

chapters.title: A documented threshold
chapters.intro: The 1980 hangar report gives the sequence a precise stopping point before the tourist-era Vieux-Port. It supports a transformation question without pretending to answer every part of it.

activations.title: Reviewed research packet
activations.use: A reusable source set for deciding which port-to-city stories deserve production.
activations.dependency: Final rights check and frame-level review of report-sequence records.

activations.title: Cross-scale evidence walk
activations.use: Move from aerial context to rue de la Commune, then back to the working shoreline and its later transition.
activations.dependency: On-site viewpoint validation before route claims are published.

activations.title: Source-linked editorial system
activations.use: Every public caption can retain its canonical ID, archive wording, source and unresolved questions.

nextStep: Complete the release gates, then test the same evidence core with one Old Port decision owner and one SDC decision owner.
